# dsh-toomuch-plugins
**Makes room in the DSH Web sidebar.** · *Too many plugins, too little room.*
English | 简体中文

A small plugin set that gives the DeepSeek Harness
(DSH) Web sidebar some breathing room.
It ships one plugin today:
| Plugin | What it does |
| Sidebar panel collapse | Collapses the "global panels" column above the workspace into one toggle
in the sidebar footer, plus a display settings page |
## Why

The DSH Web sidebar stacks, from top to bottom: brand row → new session → **global
panel entries** →
workspace → settings.

Every plugin that adds a sidebar entry adds a row to that column: plugins, plugin
market, schedules,

MCP studio, context, skill manager, system monitor… Seven rows
are roughly 280px, which squeezes th
e workspace region down to a few sessions.

This plugin does exactly one thing: **collapse that column of global panel
entries**, and bring it b
ack when you need it.
## Highlights

- **Collapsed by default** — the workspace gets ~280px back as soon as the plugin
is installed.
- **

One toggle** in the sidebar footer, right above "settings".
- **Remembered** in `localStorage`; surv

ives reloads and restarts.
- **Nothing else is touched** — no panel, no workspace, no host behaviour

; only
the display of the list element the sidebar already renders.
- **Themed** with `--dsw-alias-*

` tokens only, so it follows the DSH theme.
- **Rail-friendly** — in the narrow 56px rail the toggle

becomes a round icon button.
- **Grid display** — in Settings → Built-in plugins, switch the entry

list to icons
only (panel names become hover tooltips) with 2–4 icons per row. Bundles that skip
the

panel-list slot and inject their own sidebar buttons (the `data-dsh-*-entry`
convention, e.g. 今日值得读

/ 全局搜索 / 容器) are adopted into the grid too, and
put back in place when the grid turns off.
- **Keep

some entries while collapsed** — list mode keeps the first 0–5 entries
visible while the panels are

collapsed; grid mode keeps the first 0–3 rows
(rows × icons). Default 0, i.e. everything collapsed.

- **Plugin display order** — pick panels one by one from a dropdown on the
settings page; the list

order is the sidebar order (lossless CSS `order`
overrides). Capped at 20, duplicates dropped on sav

e. The dropdown also
lists slot-skipping sidebar entries (今日值得读 / 全局搜索 / 容器 and other
`data-dsh-*-en

try` followers); listed ones are adopted into the list so the
order really applies, and released whe

n the order is cleared.
- **Click counting** — panel clicks accumulate into
`~/.dsh/plugins/dsh-toom

uch-plugins/click-counts.json`, (silently skipped when the remote is unavailable).
- **Icon size** —

pick small (12px), medium (the sidebar's own size, the
default) or large (24px); the list and grid

the preference lives in `localStorage`
alongside the collapse state and survives reloads.

## Install

The plugin is a repository-root package: it declares the `dsh.bundle` manifest, so
DSH can install i
t straight from npm or GitHub.

s plugin settings (it is written into the profile's
`dsh.profile.bundles`), then refresh the page.

From the plugin market, once listed: open **Settings → Plugin Market** in DSH and
search for `dsh-to

market, once listed: open **Settings → Plugin Market** in DSH and
search for `dsh-toomuch-plugins`.

**Verify:** the sidebar footer gains a "Collapse global panels / Expand global
panels" row above "se

ttings", and the global panel column is gone. Settings →
Built-in plugins gains a "Sidebar panel dis

play" page for grid mode,
icons-per-row, how many entries (list) or rows (grid) stay visible while
c

ollapsed, the custom plugin display order (up to 20 entries), and the icon
size (small / medium / la

size (small / medium / large).
Requirements: DSH (DeepSeek Harness) with a `web` profile; Node.js ≥ 20.
## How it works
`src/client.js` does the following:

1. registers a toggle into the sidebar footer slot `sidebar.footer.action` (the
row next to "setting

ettings page through the `settings.plugins.tab` slot (Settings →
Built-in plugins) where grid mode,

mode to the same `<nav>`: a marker class plus a columns CSS
variable, the label span hidden, and ea

ch entry's `aria-label` mirrored into
the native `title` as the hover tooltip (DSH's own tooltip is

play order as CSS `order` overrides on the `<nav>`'s
direct children (lossless — React's DOM reconci

ts a hand-rolled Typert remote contribution (the dsh-cost-meter pattern)
and reports panel clicks to

the host half, which accumulates them into
`click-counts.json` .

The host half (`src/index.js`) only provides that one `spcClicks` service:
a prototype method plus a

written-out `typertRemote` binding, picked up by the
gateway's src-descriptor fallback — no generat
ed manifest, no DSH internals.

The basis is DSH's own `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar`: `nav.panelList` is a
direct child of th

e sidebar root, so walking up from the footer button always
reaches it. Styling uses only `--dsw-ali

as-*` theme variables, and the stylesheet
rides inside the component, so unmounting removes it.
